correctness.rationale: The two original alternating categorical product laws share exactly one 2m-string (C,A)^m of equal mass t^m, hence their JS=(1-t^m)log2. Grouping homogenized A/C words by count produces exact entropy defect H_m=(1/2)sum_{k=0}^{2m}h(a_mk,b_mk). Its m=1 expansion gives Delta_1=(3/4)log(4/3)t+O(t²log(1/t))>0 near zero. For any fixed t∈(0,1), choosing k=m+floor(cm) for small c>0 makes BOTH word-type probabilities decay exponentially slower than t^m: Stirling exponents -I(c)+(1-c)log(2-t)+c log t and -I(c)-c log t are positive. Since h(a,b)>=2log2*min(a,b) and equal-ratio words can be grouped, H_m>t^m log2 eventually, thus Delta_m<0. Independently recomputed high-precision finite entropy defects at t=.1: m=1 +.00698573, m=2 +.000216649, m=3 -.0000692693, m=4 -.00002007175; inspected exact Fraction logarithm verifier.
residual_risks: Finite computations corroborate only m<=4; asymptotic sign follows separate Stirling argument.
